If a checkout has a stale local `main` while `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` points at `origin/main` (or a local branch with the same name), this selects the wrong base and can produce an incorrect merge-base/diff. The resolved base is not passed to `runCoverage` below, so an explicit `--base` or `MAINA_BASE` is used by the diff filter but ignored by diff-cover, which independently resolves the repository default. Pass this `baseBranch` through to the coverage invocation so all pipeline tools compare against the same base ref.

An empty string here does not distinguish a clean diff from a failed Git command: `exec` converts every non-zero Git exit to `""`. In a newly initialized repository with no commit, `resolveBaseBranch` returns `HEAD` and both `git diff HEAD` calls fail, so this branch returns every finding and still falls open—the exact guardrail this change is intended to prevent. Preserve command success/failure

`runCoverage` is invoked by `runPipeline` without passing the pipeline's resolved `baseBranch` (the only call supplies only `cwd` and `available`). Consequently `maina verify --base develop` or `MAINA_BASE=develop` filters normal findings against `develop` but runs diff-cover against its own default branch, so coverage results are inconsistent with the requested scope. The docs/commentary here describe `.maina/ignore` as “gitignore-style” and claim patterns like `foo/bar` are a “substring match” and `foo/*.js` are “directory prefix + suffix”. The actual matcher behaves differently from gitignore semantics (e.g., `foo/*.js` will also match deeper paths like `foo/bar/baz.js`, and `foo/bar` is treated more like a path-segment match than an arbitrary substring). The subsequent `prior.referrer` / `prior.landing_path` accesses will then throw and cause the whole capture block to no-op (swallowed by the outer try/catch). Consider normalizing `prior` to `{}` when it’s falsy or not a plain object before reading prop

The comment says rewriting the mailto action “works for the JS-disabled path”, but this logic only runs with JS enabled. Either adjust the wording or (if needed) move attribution into the server-rendered `mailtoHref` (which likely isn’t possible with sessionStorage-based capture).

`refreshMailtoAction()` only updates the form’s `action`, but the visible fallback link uses a separate `…` and won’t include attribution. To ensure attribution makes it through when the fetch path fails, also rewrite the fallback anchor’s `href` (or derive it from the updated form action).

`readAttribution()` can return `null` if `sessionStorage.maina_attrib` was set to the JSON literal `null` (JSON.parse('null') is valid). Call sites then do `Object.keys(a)` / `attribution.utm_source`, which will throw. Consider normalizing the parsed value to a plain object (e.g., `if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed)) return {}`) before returning.

`mkdirSync(join(target, ".."), { recursive: true })` is not a safe way to create the parent directory for a file path. Because it treats the filename as a path segment, it can fail with ENOENT/ENOTDIR in cases where the file name component is traversed. Use `dirname(target)` (and create that) instead.
